validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED. Real, long-established pipeline. The dedicated Egypt Oil & Gas feature 'KPC 24" Abu Gharadig-Dahshour Pipeline Repair Project' describes it explicitly: 24-inch line, 7.1mm wall, built/designed 1974, runs Abu Gharadig Plant -> Dahshour Plant through mainly uninhabited desert, line-break valves along its length; operated by GUPCO then Khalda (KPC) from Feb 2011, corrosion-driven MAOP de-rating (795->690 psig). This is the Western Desert Gas Project (WDGP) South Line main trunk. GulfPub PE World Map independently carries the same pipe as 'Western Desert Gas Project - South Line' (Abu El-Gharadiq -> Dahshour, 24-in, 1974). Two independent origins agree -> existence high. CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED gas transmission trunk (rich gas from Abu Gharadig plant to Dahshour LPG/gas plant, then sales gas to GASCO); not gathering/oil/NGL/plant-internal. DUPLICATE: CLEARED within the operating-gas scope. Not a relabel of any other GEM operating row: P0476 (Salam-Abu Gharadig Southern, 18-in, ~212 km) is the upstream Salam->Abu Gharadig feeder (GulfPub 'WDGP-South Line, Salam->Abu Gharadiq GP, 18-in, 296 km'), and P0477/P6697-P6702 (South Valley) are the Dahshour->Aswan downstream continuation — different segments, not this pipe. Caveat: the '(1)' suffix implies a parallel/sister '(2)' line entered separately; none found in the operating roster (would be out-of-scope if under another status). SPEC (the concern): DIAMETER 24 in is solid (Egypt Oil & Gas + GulfPub agree). LENGTH is off: GEM=290 km but the engineering repair source states 262.5 km (Abu Gharadig Plant->Dahshour Plant) and GulfPub lists 180 km; 290 vs 262.5 is ~10% high — recommend 262.5 (most authoritative). CAPACITY 120 MMcf/d could NOT be independently corroborated (GulfPub's 300 mmcfd is its placeholder, not a real figure) — left unverified, not filled. SOURCING WEAKNESS: the row's current cited ref (miga.org Apache 2004 EIA PDF) returns 200 but does NOT contain 'Abu Gharadig', 'Dahshour', 'pipeline' or 'Khalda' on extraction — i.e. it does not verifiably name this pipeline; the real support is the Egypt Oil & Gas KPC feature. ATTRIBUTION note: operator = Khalda Petroleum Company (KPC), an Apache/Khalda-linked JV, not GASCO; GulfPub mis-attributes to BAPETCO. Owner/operator refs belong on the operators/owners tab.

routes.end_name: Dahshour gas/LPG plant (Giza governorate, SW of Cairo)
routes.corridor_desc: Roughly W-E trunk across the northern Western Desert, ~262.5 km, from the Abu Gharadig gas plant eastward through mainly uninhabited desert to the Dahshour gas/LPG plant on the Nile-valley edge SW of Cairo. Endpoints are firmly sourced and named; the desert interior is unconstrained by waypoints, so the interior path is a loose bound (essentially a desert corridor, likely tracking near the parallel WDGP North Line / Cairo-Alexandria desert corridor). Start coordinate is APPROXIMATE — bounded to the Abu Gharadig field area (~29.6-29.9N, 28.0-28.5E per published basin/field studies); Dahshour endpoint is precisely known.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the Egypt Oil & Gas KPC feature (Abu Gharadig Plant -> Dahshour Plant, 'mainly uninhabited desert'). Dahshour coord = the well-known Dahshur/Dahshour site SW of Cairo (~29.79N, 31.22E). Abu Gharadig start coord approximated to the field area from published Abu Gharadig Basin location studies (BED-3/Sitra ~29.75-30.05N/27.5-28.2E; NEAG ~29.9N/29.9E, 127 km from Cairo) — NOT a fabricated point; no exact plant coordinate was sourceable so it is left approximate. No interior waypoints could be sourced.
